newsitem.title: UK: Egypt could delay some sugar until 2nd half - trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt could delay some sugar until 2nd half - trade.

text.p: Egypt could end up delaying some of its recent raw sugar purchases until the second half of 1997 due to port congestion, London sugar sources said on Friday.
Details are as yet sketchy but traders said some international suppliers could be under pressure to find alternative destinations for their sugar.
"There are rumours about (Egypt) not being able to take all the sugar," said one European trader. "I don't to know to what extent this is concrete yet...but there is definitely talk about it."
Traders said the quantity of sugar involved was thought to be limited.

Earlier, a Cairo-based trader said Egypt's state refiner, the Sugar and Integrated Industries Company (SIIC), had asked suppliers to delay some shipments by up to four months due to a shortage of storage space.

But three or four vessels carrying about 20,000 tonnes apiece, thought to Cuban raws as part of a total 750,000 tonnes ordered for this year's delivery programme, were already on the way to Egypt, he said.
"The Egyptian domestic market is already well supplied at present so it might make sense for them to take the sugar later rather than earlier," said a London broker, citing a recent trade report.
Another broker said Egypt's limited number of berths available for unloading sugar was likely to be hampering the whole delivery programme.
"I think there are a limited number of sugar berths which could cause a slight problem," he said.
"If they get two or three vessels turning up at the same time and there's someone already on the berth you've got to start looking at grain berths."
Egypt's sugar imports mainly come from Cuba and Brazil. It also takes smaller quantities from the European Union.
According to data from the International Sugar Organization (ISO), its imports totalled 1.08 million tonnes in 1995, almost double the amount for 1994.
Egypt plans to become self-sufficient in sugar with a programme of expanded beet production and reduced raws imports.
